title: ISRO Scientist/Engineer SC Result: Civil, EE, RAC Panels Out
summary: ISRO SC panels for Civil, Electrical, RAC, Architecture (20 Nov 2026): 19 selected from 131, valid to 19 Nov 2027. Counts, eligibility, 50:50 maths.
body_markdown:
ISRO has published the selection panels for the last four Scientist/Engineer 'SC' posts in its 2026 GATE-score recruitment: Civil (ISRO and PRL), Electrical, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, and Architecture. The panels were uploaded on Friday, 20 November 2026, under advertisement ISRO:ICRB:02(EMC-CEPO):2026. They select 19 candidates for 19 posts and wait-list others. Each panel is valid up to 19 November 2027. The selected engineers join at Level 10 of the pay matrix, on a minimum basic pay of ₹


56,100 a month.


The Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science panels from the same advertisement came out on 5 and 13 November, so this upload completes the cycle. Below are the numbers for each discipline, what the panels confirm and what they leave out, a worked example of the 50:50 GATE-plus-interview weighting, and a prep plan for anyone aiming at the next cycle.


## Key facts at a glance


- **What:** the selection panels (results of the interviews) for post codes BE004 and BE004A (Civil, ISRO and PRL), BE005 (Electrical), BE006 (Refrigeration and Air Conditioning) and BE007 (Architecture). ISRO's notice page calls these the "CEPO posts". The four PDFs are dated 20 November 2026 and are posted on the[ICRB 02(EMC-CEPO):2026 page](https://www.isro.gov.in/ICRB_Recruitment12.html) .
- **Selections:** Civil 11 (10 ISRO + 1 PRL), Electrical 4, Refrigeration and AC 2, Architecture 2. Every advertised CEPO post has a selected candidate.
- **Competition:** ISRO called 131 candidates to interview for these 19 posts. About 1 in 7 was selected.
- **Whole 2026 GATE route:** 631 candidates were called for 92 posts and 87 were selected. The 5 unfilled posts were all reserved for PwBD candidates (3 in Electronics, 2 in Mechanical).
- **Validity:** all four panels say "THE PANEL IS VALID UPTO 19.11.2027". Wait-listed candidates can be offered a post until then if a selected candidate doesn't join.


Skill-Lync's permanent[ISRO Scientist/Engineer page](https://skill-lync.com/isro-scientist-engineer) tracks both ISRO recruitment routes, the GATE route and the written test, in one place. When we last checked it on 16 November 2026, it listed these four panels as awaited. This post covers the 20 November panels, which are newer.


## What exactly did ISRO publish on 20 November 2026?


ISRO's Centralised Recruitment Board (ICRB) uploaded four selection panels under the heading "Results of the interviews for CEPO posts". There is one panel each for Civil (ISRO and PRL), Electrical, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, and Architecture. Each panel lists, by category, who is selected and who is wait-listed. Each closes with the line that the panel is valid up to 19 November 2027.


The PDFs carry 20 November 2026 in their file names. Their internal creation times are 5:15 to 5:22 PM IST that day, and the server's Last-Modified time for the Civil file is 5:51 PM IST. The news item that flagged this was timestamped 6:08 PM IST. The "CEPO" label comes from the advertisement. CEPO is the Civil Engineering Programme Office at ISRO Headquarters in Bengaluru. Together with the construction and maintenance divisions at each centre, it plans, designs, builds and maintains ISRO's ground structures, buildings and facilities.


**Confirmed vs not stated.** Everything in this post comes from ISRO's own documents: the 28 July 2026 advertisement, the 29 September interview schedules and the four 20 November panels. We read all of them on 22 November 2026. The panels list only a position (1, 2, WL-1 and so on) for each candidate. They don't give marks, the final aggregate, the GATE cut-off for these disciplines, the posting centre or a joining date. ISRO published GATE-score cut-offs for Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science only. We don't name any candidate in this post.


## How many candidates were selected in each discipline?


ISRO selected 19 candidates for the 19 CEPO posts: 10 for Civil at ISRO plus 1 for Civil at PRL, 4 for Electrical, 2 for Refrigeration and Air Conditioning and 2 for Architecture. The panels also carry 33 wait-list entries. In each discipline, the number selected in every category equals the number of posts the advertisement reserved for that category.

Counted from ISRO's four panel PDFs of 20 November 2026 and the interview schedules of 29 September 2026. UR is unreserved, OBC is Other Backward Classes, SC/ST are Scheduled Castes/Tribes and EWS is Economically Weaker Sections. None of these four posts had a PwBD reservation.


Some names appear on more than one list, and reading the panels correctly depends on this:


- **"Selected under general merit."** An OBC candidate who scores high enough to make the unreserved list is shown on the OBC list with this remark. They don't use up an OBC post, so the next OBC candidate gets it. This happens once in Civil and once in Refrigeration and AC.
- **Wait-list entries that are already selected elsewhere.** In Civil, two people on the unreserved wait-list are selected on the OBC list, and one of them is also on the PRL wait-list. In Electrical, the first unreserved wait-list entry is the OBC selection. Leaving out these entries, the 33 wait-list entries cover 27 different candidates who have not been selected.
- **One person tops both Civil lists.** The first-ranked unreserved candidate for Civil at ISRO is also the one selected for Civil at PRL, under a separate registration number. They can join only one, so one of the two lists will probably have to go to its wait-list. That is our reading of the panels; ISRO doesn't comment on it.


## How does this complete ISRO's 2026 GATE-route recruitment?


With these four panels out, all seven post codes in advertisement ICRB:02(EMC-CEPO):2026 have a selection panel. Across the advertisement, ISRO called 631 candidates to interview for 92 posts and selected 87. The 5 posts left unfilled were reserved for candidates with benchmark disabilities: 3 in Electronics and 2 in Mechanical.


Interview calls, posts and selections for all seven post codes. The Civil, Electrical, Refrigeration and AC and Architecture rows come from the 20 November panels; the Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science rows come from the 5 and 13 November panels, as recorded on the[ISRO Scientist/Engineer page](https://skill-lync.com/isro-scientist-engineer) .


The advertisement asked ICRB to call candidates to interview in the ratio of 1:7, and the interview lists follow it closely. Civil called 6.7 candidates per post, Electrical 7.0, Refrigeration and AC 7.5 and Architecture 7.0. Selected candidates made up 13.3% to 14.9% of those interviewed in each CEPO discipline, and 13.8% across all seven post codes.


The timing was steady too. Each discipline's panel came out 21 to 29 days after its last interview day: 21 days for Mechanical, 28 for Computer Science and 29 for Electronics, then 21 to 23 days for the four CEPO posts. From the advertisement on 28 July to the last panels on 20 November took 115 days.


The two tracks of ICRB:02(EMC-CEPO):2026. Dates are from ISRO's notice page, the interview schedules and the panel PDFs.


## Who was eligible for these posts?


All four posts needed a bachelor's degree in the discipline with at least 65% aggregate marks (the average of all semesters) or a CGPA of 6.84 on a 10-point scale. Candidates also needed a valid GATE 2025 or GATE 2026 score in the matching paper. The upper age limit was 28 years on 17 August 2026, with relaxation for reserved categories where posts were reserved.


Post Degree GATE paper Tentative centres in the advertisement


Civil (BE004) BE/BTech in Civil Engineering CE IPRC (Mahendragiri), ISRO HQ, ISTRAC and URSC (Bengaluru), SDSC SHAR (Sriharikota), VSSC (Thiruvananthapuram), LPSC (Valiamala), NRSC (Hyderabad)


Civil, PRL (BE004A) BE/BTech in Civil Engineering CE PRL, Ahmedabad (an autonomous body; Group A non-gazetted)


Electrical (BE005) BE/BTech in Electrical, or Electrical and Electronics EE NRSC (Hyderabad), SAC (Ahmedabad)


Refrigeration and AC (BE006) BE/BTech in Mechanical, with air conditioning and refrigeration (or allied subjects) as an elective or core subject in any semester ME SAC (Ahmedabad)


Architecture (BE007) Bachelor's in Architecture plus a valid Council of Architecture registration AR URSC (Bengaluru), VSSC (Thiruvananthapuram)


The age cut-offs by date of birth were: UR and EWS candidates born on or after 18 August 1998, OBC on or after 18 August 1995, and SC/ST on or after 18 August 1993. The application fee was ₹


250. Women, SC, ST, ex-servicemen and PwBD candidates paid nothing. Applications ran from 28 July to 17 August 2026, and the fee could be paid until 19 August.


Two eligibility rules catch people out. First, if a university's degree certificate shows only a CGPA, ISRO won't convert it to a percentage, even when the university publishes a formula. Second, ISRO shortlists on the GATE score you type into the form. That means the score out of 1,000, not your marks or rank, and ICRB checks it.


## How does ISRO combine the GATE score and the interview?


ISRO shortlists for interview on GATE score alone, at about 7 candidates per post. The final panel then gives 50% weight to the GATE score and 50% to interview marks out of 100. To make the panel, an unreserved or EWS candidate needs at least 50% in GATE, 50 in the interview and a 60% aggregate. Reserved candidates need 40%, 40 and 50%.


The interview is marked out of 100:


- technical (academic) knowledge, 40 marks
- general awareness of your area of specialisation, 20
- presentation and communication, 20
- comprehension, 10
- academic achievements, 10


The academic achievements marks come from a fixed formula:


- **Institute:** 3 marks for an IIT, IISc, IIST, an NIT or an NIRF top-20 institute.
- **Grades:** 4 marks for a CGPA above 9 (or above 85%), and 2 for a CGPA of 7.5 to 9 (or 71% to 85%).
- **Rank:** 3 marks for an institute rank of 1 to 3.


So an NIT graduate with a CGPA of 8.2 and no rank starts with 5 of these 10 marks. A state-college graduate with a CGPA of 9.1 and an institute rank of 2 starts with 7.


### Worked example: does a higher GATE score always win?


The advertisement says "50% weightage" but doesn't say how a GATE score out of 1,000 is turned into a percentage. The natural reading is to divide by 10, and that is the assumption here. Candidate A has a GATE score of 780 and 58 interview marks. Candidate B has a GATE score of 690 and 70 interview marks. Both clear the unreserved floors, and B ranks above A even though A's GATE score is 90 points higher. Under this reading, each interview mark is worth 10 GATE-score points. B's 12-mark lead in the interview is worth 120 GATE points, more than A's 90-point lead.


The floors interact in a way that is easy to miss. At the minimum interview mark of 50, an unreserved candidate needs a GATE score of 700 just to reach the 60% aggregate. For comparison, ISRO's 2026 GATE-score cut-offs for the interview list were 719 for Mechanical, 690 for Electronics and 827 for Computer Science (unreserved). A Mechanical candidate exactly at the 719 cut-off who scores the minimum 50 in the interview would reach 60.95, less than one mark above the floor and well below candidates A and B. Near the shortlisting cut-off, a pass-mark interview is not enough to rank.


The qualifying floors in the advertisement, drawn on a GATE-score versus interview plane, with lines of equal aggregate. The divide-by-10 conversion is our reading; ISRO doesn't state it. The numbers are re-computed by the script in this post's run folder.


## What is the salary of an ISRO Scientist/Engineer 'SC'?


Scientist/Engineer 'SC' is a Group A post at Level 10 of the 7th Pay Commission pay matrix. The minimum basic pay is ₹


56,100 a month. Dearness Allowance, House Rent Allowance and Transport Allowance are paid on top, as per the rules in force. Appointees come under the National Pension System or the Unified Pension Scheme.


The advertisement also lists medical cover for the employee and dependants, a subsidised canteen, limited quarters (in place of HRA), Leave Travel Concession, group insurance and house-building advance. Promotion runs on ISRO's Merit Promotion Scheme. Under it, promotion for scientific and technical posts doesn't depend on a vacancy opening up, and is decided by periodic performance reviews. We have not converted this into a monthly in-hand figure: allowances depend on the city of posting and the DA rate at the time of joining.


## What happens next if you are selected or wait-listed?


ISRO hasn't published a joining schedule. The advertisement says offers and all other communication go by email and through the ISRO website, so selected candidates should watch their registered email, including the spam folder. The advertisement also says appointees can be posted to, and later transferred to, any ISRO or Department of Space centre. The centres in the table above are only tentative.


If you are wait-listed, your chance depends on how many selected candidates decline. Past ISRO panels show this varies a lot. In the 2023 written-test cycle, the Mechanical wait-list moved to WL-53 and the Computer Science list to WL-18, while Electronics had no wait-list at all. These figures are recorded with their sources on the[ISRO Scientist/Engineer page](https://skill-lync.com/isro-scientist-engineer) . That was a different recruitment route, so don't read these numbers as a forecast for the CEPO panels.


## When is the next ISRO Scientist/Engineer recruitment?


ISRO hasn't announced the next GATE-route advertisement. The 2026 one was dated 28 July 2026 and accepted GATE 2025 or GATE 2026 scores. Whether a 2027 advertisement will accept GATE 2027 scores, and which disciplines it will include, isn't known yet.


The written-test route is separate. Under advertisement ISRO:ICRB:03(EMC):2026, the computer-based test for Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science was held on 29 October 2026. The window for objections to the answer keys closed on 15 November, and the results are awaited. That route is open only to Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science graduates. For Civil, Electrical and Architecture graduates, the GATE route was the only ICRB route in 2026.


GATE 2027, conducted by IIT Madras, runs on 6, 7, 13, 14, 20 and 21 February 2027, with results due on 19 March 2027. See our[GATE 2027 exam dates](https://skill-lync.com/gate/exam-dates) page for the full schedule.


## How should Civil, Electrical and Mechanical (RAC) graduates prepare for the next cycle?


Treat it as two exams. Your GATE score gets you into the interview, and the interview then decides half your final marks. A plan that works around GATE 2027:


1. **Now to February 2027: get the GATE score as high as you can.** Shortlisting is on the score alone. Use the paper-wise pages for[GATE Civil](https://skill-lync.com/gate/civil) ,[GATE Electrical](https://skill-lync.com/gate/electrical) and[GATE Mechanical](https://skill-lync.com/gate/mechanical) (the paper for the Refrigeration and AC post), and our[GATE 2027 study plan](https://skill-lync.com/blogs/gate-2027-study-plan) . Check past cut-offs on the[Civil](https://skill-lync.com/gate/cutoff/civil) ,[Electrical](https://skill-lync.com/gate/cutoff/electrical) and[Mechanical](https://skill-lync.com/gate/cutoff/mechanical) cut-off pages.
2. **Check your eligibility early.** Confirm your aggregate (at least 65%, or a CGPA of 6.84) on the marks sheet itself, not through a conversion formula. Check your age against the cut-off date. If you are aiming at the Refrigeration and AC post, make sure refrigeration and air conditioning appears as an elective or core subject in your transcript.
3. **March to the interview: prepare for the 40-mark technical section.** Pick the 3 or 4 subjects you are strongest in and be ready to work problems on a whiteboard. For Civil, that might be RCC and steel design, soil mechanics and foundations, and construction planning. For Electrical, power systems, machines and protection. For Refrigeration and AC, thermodynamics, refrigeration cycles, psychrometry and load estimation.
4. **Prepare for the 20-mark "awareness of your area of specialisation" section.** Know what the post does at ISRO. Civil engineers in CEPO plan, design, build and maintain buildings and ground facilities. Read your discipline's codes and current practice, not space trivia.
5. **Keep other options open alongside.** The same GATE score feeds PSU recruitment. Track it on[GATE PSU recruitment](https://skill-lync.com/gate/psu-recruitment) . For defence R&D, see[DRDO Scientist 'B'](https://skill-lync.com/drdo-scientist-b) .


If you want structured practice in the design work behind these interviews, Skill-Lync has courses on[analysis and design of buildings](https://skill-lync.com/civil-engineering-courses/analysis-design-buildings-professional-approach) ,[HVAC systems and flow analysis](https://skill-lync.com/mechanical-engineering-courses/hvac-systems-flow-analysis) and[electric power systems](https://skill-lync.com/electrical-engineering-courses/introduction-electric-power-system) .


## What does this mean for engineering students?


ISRO hires a handful of Civil, Electrical, Refrigeration and AC and Architecture engineers each cycle: 19 posts in 2026, against 73 across Electronics, Mechanical and Computer Science. With about 7 candidates called per post, everyone on the interview list already has a strong GATE score. From there, the interview counts for as much as the score. And because the published lists show only a position for each candidate, never marks, ISRO's notices don't tell you what final aggregate was enough to get in.


So a strong GATE score, a clean eligibility record and a well-prepared technical interview are what count. These panels show the posts get filled, category by category, about three weeks after the interviews end.


## Frequently asked questions


### Is the ISRO Scientist/Engineer SC result for Civil and Electrical out?


Yes. ISRO published the selection panels for Civil (ISRO and PRL), Electrical, Refrigeration and Air Conditioning, and Architecture on 20 November 2026, under advertisement ISRO:ICRB:02(EMC-CEPO):2026. They are on ISRO's ICRB 02(EMC-CEPO):2026 notice page.


### How many Civil engineers did ISRO select in 2026?


Eleven: 10 for ISRO (UR 3, OBC 2, SC 2, ST 1, EWS 2) and 1 for the Physical Research Laboratory (UR), out of 74 candidates called to interview. The same candidate ranks first on both the ISRO and PRL lists, so one of those offers will likely pass to the wait-list.


### Does ISRO publish marks or cut-offs with the selection panel?


Not for these posts. The panels show only each candidate's position and whether they are selected or wait-listed. ISRO published GATE-score cut-offs for the interview list only for Electronics (690), Mechanical (719) and Computer Science (827), for unreserved candidates.


### Can a Mechanical engineer apply for the ISRO Refrigeration and AC post?


Yes, if refrigeration and air conditioning (or an allied subject) was an elective or core subject in any semester of your Mechanical degree. You also need a valid GATE score in the Mechanical paper (ME) and at least 65% aggregate or a CGPA of 6.84.


### How long is an ISRO selection panel valid?


These four panels are valid up to 19 November 2027, one year from publication. Wait-listed candidates can be offered a post during that time if selected candidates do not join.
